name: inofull
description: A CREATE THAT FAILS FOR WANT OF INODES MUST NOT LEAVE THE DIRECTORY LOCKED.  disk/ufsfewino.po has 45 inodes in total, so it is permanently under NICINOD (100) free and every ufs_ialloc on it takes the rescan-from-the-top path; filling it past 45 files drives the create-fails-with-ENOSPC arm, which nothing else in the suite reaches.  THE ASSERTION IS THAT THE MACHINE IS STILL THERE.  vn_open takes LOCKPARENT and this tree's ufs_maknode never touches ni_dvp -- the caller owns it, unlike Reno where maknode ends with iput(pdir) -- so a failing create that returns early leaves the parent locked by a process that has moved on, and the next lookup descending into it waits for a lock it already owns.  MEASURED BOTH WAYS: before the fix this run ended `f6: cannot create' then `lockself 0002' and PANIC, naming the mount point's own inode; after it, the fill reports its errors and the shell answers.  apple/fgx#278.  The needle is built by shell expansion (Z=ok; echo ALIVE=$Z) so the typed line cannot contain it, and the fill lines are kept SHORT: a 150-character `for' left the shell with no prompt and every later line merely echoed, which is a dropped keystroke (apple/fgx#265) and not a filesystem result.
